title: Combining thermal hydrolysis and methylation-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to characterise complex organic assemblages in geological material
author: Purvis, Sano, et al.
materials: Nitrile gloves were worn at all times and flamed forceps were used for handling samples according to the procedure described in [2]. Solid sections of rock were cut from the internal volume of parent samples to remove the outer 5–10 mm. The sections were trimmed into billets that were ca. 10 mm2 × 5 mm. All sample cutting was carried out on a Buehler Isomet 1000, cutting wheel (Buehler AG, Uzwil, Switzerland). Any moisture in the geological samples was removed by freeze-drying for 48 h in a Thermo Modulyo D0230 (Sciquip ltd., Shropshire, UK), for example from the calcareous foraminifer ooze studied in [1]. The geological samples were then cleaned using UV/O3 for 20 min, using a Jelight-144AX UV/O3 cleanertm (Jelight Co Inc., Irvine, CA, United States) [3,4] and subsequently stored in glass vials (sealed with UV/O3 cleaned Al foil under screw top lids).

For conventional flash pyrolysis, the quartz tubes were immediately loaded into a CDS 1000 pyroprobe unit (CDS Analytical, USA). For THM-GC/MS analysis, 2 μl of 25%v/v TMAH (Sigma-Aldrich, UK) in double distilled water was added directly onto the samples in the quartz tube using a glass syringe before insertion into the pyroprobe unit. The maximum pyrolysis temperatures were set to either 450 °C, 610 °C and 1000 °C (see additional information). The pyrolysis temperature was maintained for 10 s (20 °C ms−1 temperature ramp) using a pulsed-mode open pyrolysis system, fitted with a platinum coil.

Solid rock billets were de-gassed for 48 h, prior to XPS analysis using a Thermo Modulyo D0230 freeze drier without using refrigeration, to reduce the time the XPS instrument required to obtain the ultra-high vacuum essential for the analysis. The de-gassed samples were placed directly onto the instrument analysis plate where they were immobilised by clips.

steps.title: Cut and size geological samples
steps.instruction: Wear nitrile gloves and use flamed forceps to cut solid sections from the interior of rock cores, removing the outer 5–10 mm; trim the sections into billets approximately 10 mm² × 5 mm using a Buehler Isomet 1000 cutting wheel.

steps.title: Remove moisture by freeze‑drying
steps.instruction: Place the billets in a Thermo Modulyo D0230 freeze‑drier and dry for 48 h to eliminate all moisture.

steps.title: UV/O₃ clean and store samples
steps.instruction: Clean each dried billet in a Jelight‑144AX UV/O₃ cleaner for 20 min, then store them in glass vials sealed with UV/O₃‑cleaned aluminium foil under screw‑top lids.

steps.title: Mill, sieve, and load samples for GC/MS
steps.instruction: Hand‑mill the cleaned solid rock billets in a UV/O₃‑cleaned agate pestle and mortar, pass the powder through a 150 µm stainless‑steel screen that has been flamed to 750 °C, weigh approximately 10 mg of the resulting material into a clean quartz pyrolysis tube and plug the tube with extracted silica wool. Fine‑grained material may be used directly without further preparation.

substeps.instruction: Mill billets in UV/O₃‑cleaned agate mortar.
Plug tube with extracted silica wool.

steps.title: Add TMAH for THM‑GC/MS (optional)
steps.instruction: For THM‑GC/MS, dispense 2 µL of 25 % v/v tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH, Sigma‑Aldrich, UK) prepared in double‑distilled water onto the sample in the quartz tube using a glass syringe; for conventional flash pyrolysis, load the tube directly into the CDS 1000 pyroprobe.

substeps.instruction: Load tube into CDS 1000 pyroprobe for flash pyrolysis (no additive).
Add 2 µL of 25 % v/v TMAH solution to tube for THM‑GC/MS.

steps.title: Set pyrolysis parameters and run
steps.instruction: Program the pyroprobe to a maximum temperature of 450 °C, 610 °C or 1000 °C as required, ramp at 20 °C ms⁻¹, hold the target temperature for 10 s, and perform the run in pulsed‑mode open pyrolysis using a platinum coil.

substeps.instruction: Run using pulsed‑mode open pyrolysis with platinum coil.

steps.title: Degas solid billets for XPS
steps.instruction: Place solid rock billets in the Thermo Modulyo D0230 freeze‑drier (without refrigeration) for 48 h to degas, then mount each degassed billet directly onto the XPS analysis plate and immobilise with clips.

steps.title: Compact fine‑grained material onto Al foil for XPS
steps.instruction: Cut a 30 mm² piece of aluminium foil, fold it into an approximate 10 mm diameter disk, place the disk in a KBr pellet press, add the fine‑grained geological material on top, apply 1.5 t m⁻² pressure using a manual hydraulic press (Specac Ltd.), then attach the compacted disc to the XPS analysis plate with 3 M double‑sided carbon tape.

substeps.instruction: Cut 30 mm² Al foil and fold into ~10 mm disk.
Insert foil disk into KBr pellet press apparatus.
Add fine‑grained sample onto foil surface.
Apply 1.5 t m⁻² pressure with manual hydraulic press.
Attach resulting disc to XPS plate using 3 M carbon tape.
